pr_title: Fix timers running inside scene preview on drag
pr_body:
This PR closes #39221.

~~As a hacky work-around, we iterate through all first-level children of the scene's root and call `stop()` on the ones that are Timers.~~

~~This approach is bad, and I'm currently thinking of using the pause function of the scene tree, but for some reason Godot crashes when toggling pause, which I'll need to investigate.~~

New approach is to pause the subtree which starts with the node containing the preview, instead of iterating through all of its children. This ensures that the preview stays frozen regardless of the existence of second-level timers (unless the child nodes are set to `Process` pause mode) and is cleaner than the old one, IMO.

(This is not a duplicate PR, the old one was not based on the `master` branch due to an oversight of mine)

EDIT: Waiting for the `OS/DisplayServer` split to be completed ~~(or at least previews working again on master)~~
Previews are working again, so this is ready for review.
pr_comments:
pausing scene preview is not good I think.
it is helpful when placing particle scene or etc.
@volzhs I don't know if this is intended behavior, paging @Calinou

I just set up test scene to demonstrate it.
![instance_scene](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8281454/83529921-fae66e80-a525-11ea-9e05-7ce54ad279e4.gif)
it is pretty helpful with viewing live update instanced scene.
Do we want this as a feature or should I fix it? @Calinou @KoBeWi
The fix itself isn't really complicated, so unless the issue is really unimportant, it should be ok to have this (but I wonder if there are other nodes that could be taken care of too).

> The fix itself isn't really complicated, so unless the issue is really unimportant, it should be ok to have this (but I wonder if there are other nodes that could be taken care of too).

I didn't quite get what you mean here: by "this" you mean to have the behavior after the fix, or the behavior as it is now? If we want the current behavior this issue can be closed.

Sorry for the long delay reviewing this further. The current implementation seems OK from a cursory look, though I'm not convinced if the actual "bug" being fixed is something that needs to be fixed in the first place - but I don't have a strong opinion either way.

If @KoBeWi approves the implementation this can likely be rebased to squash the commits and solve merge conflicts, and merged.

tbh I'm not sure myself if it's worth fixing; I opened the issue because the behavior was unexpected to me. I just checked and freeing the preview node doesn't cause crash, so the issue is rather harmless.
I'd say let's shelve it for now, and revisit if we find it to actually be a problem worth fixing.

issue_context.title: Timers run inside scene drag preview
issue_context.body:

**Godot version:**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->
3.2.2 beta3

**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
This is more funny bug than critical, but when you drag a scene over viewport, any Timer in that scene will run inside the preview. I discovered it when my timer connected to AnimationPlayer made the preview animated (lol).
![15jfhsY9sp](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/83408886-a94dbf00-a413-11ea-8671-a6a94240424a.gif)
(the cursor seems to be off on the GIF for some reason, ignore it)

Luckily connecting the Timer to `queue_free()` doesn't crash the editor (just makes the preview disappear xd), so it's a rather minor bug.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[ReproductionProject.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4711224/ReproductionProject.zip)
comments: Can reproduce on freshly compiled build of 3.2.2 beta3 on Linux (Arch). However, `master` doesn't exhibit this behavior (but I see no preview there, weirdly)
@lightspot21 `master` has had its windowing system rewritten from scratch, so some features may be missing. See #37734.
As discussed in #39232, let's shelve it for now, and revisit if we find it to actually be a problem worth fixing.

review_comments: After the pause rework, you no longer need to pause the tree, just set `process_mode` of the `preview_node` to `PROCESS_NODE_DISABLED`. It will only stop the preview node, making the solution a one-liner.
